Change c0131. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): And how, Victor, can I relate our misfortune?

1818 text: Absence cannot have rendered you callous to our joys and griefs; and how shall I inflict pain on an absent child? I wish to prepare you for the woeful news, but I know it is impossible; even now your eye skims over the page, to seek the words which are to convey to you the horrible tidings.

1831 text: Absence cannot have rendered you callous to our joys and griefs; and how shall I inflict pain on my long absent son? I wish to prepare you for the woful news, but I know it is impossible; even now your eye skims over the page, to seek the words which are to convey to you the horrible tidings.

Diff: Absence cannot have rendered you callous to our joys and griefs; and how shall I inflict pain on [-an-] {+my long+} absent [-child-] {+son+} ? I wish to prepare you for the [-woeful-] {+woful+} news, but I know it is impossible; even now your eye skims over the page, to seek the words which are to convey to you the horrible tidings.

Context after (unchanged): "William is dead!—that sweet child, whose smiles delighted and warmed my heart, who was so gentle, yet so gay!

result.rationale: Replacing "an absent child" with "my long absent son" personalizes the addressee as Elizabeth's son and stresses the long separation; "woeful" becomes "woful" (spelling only).
